consequence: The sub-linear decode amortization is not the GEMV decode preference. Remaining constraint set: not prefill (C3 is 1.47x on the same prefill cost), not the decode route flag. Next measurement is a kernel-trace comparison of decode at C1 vs C2 to find which kernel families scale with rows; per-step cost goes 33.2 ms -> 50.4 ms from C1 to C2, and a weight-bound batched step should stay near 33 ms.
control: The route value is resolved once per session, not per step: the wrapper logged exactly 3 calls, all incoming=True, all resolved=False. So the flip demonstrably reached the resolver. Baseline and candidate ran through the identical driver, which installs the wrapper in both arms so the monkeypatch is not a variable.
instrument_notes: Two guards shaped the method, both worth keeping in mind. scripts/gguf_mtp_c1c8_server_bench.py:651 refuses to run against a dirty worktree, so the scratch-edit method used for the prefill arm is unavailable here; the flip was applied in memory at gguf_linear.gguf_gemv_decode_enabled, patching the runner namespace too because the runner imports the name directly. Precedence inside the resolver is explicit kwarg > session > env, and 11 call sites pass True explicitly, so no environment variable can override the route.
not_claimed: No rate claim is published from these arms beyond the C1/C2 medians shown, and these packets were produced by an in-memory patched driver, so they are diagnostic and stay under /tmp rather than entering the scoreboard.
protocol: scripts/gguf_mtp_c1c8_server_bench.py --widths 1,2 --expected-mtp-widths 2 (MTP cannot engage at one row, so expecting it at width 1 makes the harness report failed), HIPENGINE_EXECUTION_PROFILE=production, 10 prompts, median of 10 per width.
question: Task #14 first hypothesis: decode amortizes sub-linearly (1.52x off the weight-read ideal at C2, see 2026-08-30-w7900-q4km-decode-amortization-c2.json) because decode uses per-row GEMV kernels, so each wave row pays its own weight pass. Does turning the GEMV decode preference off change C1/C2?
why_neutral_is_explained_not_mysterious: hipengine/runtime/qwen35_gguf_runner.py:13292 feeds the resolver result into Qwen35GGUFFastPathSafety(requested_gemv_decode=...), and the two consumers of that field are disabled_wmma and disabled_gemv, both gated on is_qwen35moe. For this dense model the flag changes only a safety-record field, so neutrality is predicted by the source, and the 11 literal use_gemv_decode=True call sites are inert on the dense GGUF path.
